messages.author: 586289eef537a7a4
messages.subject: Clang and isnan compile error?
parts:
Hi,

 

I have a TMB code which has been developed in a Windows environment and works perfectly well there. I was going to test it under Linux but then it would not compile and it seemed to complain about some usage of isnan(). I have a .R folder containing a Makevars file where it is specified to use clang as a compiler, i.e., CXX=clang++ as (please correct me if I’m wrong) I recall there were some issues when loading the libraries after changes had been made in the cpp-file due to the gcc compiler. However, if I remove the .R folder and compile with the default gcc it compiles fine, but then I guess it still is the issue about the libraries.

 

Any ideas of what could be the problem? I suspect it has something to do with the clang version, as I found in another post someone mentioning a clang version much higher than installed on our system.

 

We are running:

 

Ubuntu 16.04 LTS

R 3.6.2

TMB 1.7.18

Clang 3.8.0-2ubuntu4

g++ (Ubuntu 4.9.3-13ubuntu2) 4.9.3

 

Kind regards,

Tor Arne

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: Clang and isnan compile error?
parts:
If it works with GCC but your main concern is library unloading I recommend you follow the instructions here:

https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp#issues-with-library-unloading

I.e., modify your Makevars to 'CXX = g++ -fno-gnu-unique'.

You may want to test that library unloading works by running this R script:
https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/master/tmb_syntax/test_reload.R
